# QA & Test Infrastructure Engineer

**OVERVIEW OF 73 STRINGS:**

73 Strings is an innovative platform providing comprehensive data extraction, monitoring, and valuation solutions for the private capital industry. The company's AI-powered platform streamlines middle-office processes for alternative investments, enabling seamless data structuring and standardization, monitoring, and fair value estimation at the click of a button. 73 Strings serves clients globally across various strategies, including Private Equity, Growth Equity, Venture Capital, Infrastructure and Private Credit.

Our 2025 $55M Series B, the largest in the industry, was led by Goldman Sachs, with participation from Golub Capital and Hamilton Lane, with continued support from Blackstone, Fidelity International Strategic Ventures and Broadhaven Ventures.  
  
Role Summary

We’re hiring a QA and Test Infrastructure Engineer into Platform Engineering. This is not a manual testing role and it isn’t a test-writing service for other teams. You’ll build the testing platform: the frameworks, environments, data, and pipelines that let every product team test their own work quickly and trust the result.

Our platform handles financial data that ends up in valuations, LP reports, and audit files. A regression that reaches production is expensive in a way that a bug in most SaaS products isn’t. At the same time we ship fast, and slow or flaky tests are the most reliable way to make engineers stop caring about tests altogether. Your job sits exactly in that tension.

You’ll sit alongside our Cloud Infrastructure and SRE engineers in Platform Engineering, sharing the same CI/CD estate, Kubernetes platform, and multi-cloud footprint across Azure, AWS, and GCP. You’ll own the testing half of that platform.

We’re hiring at mid-level and senior. What differs is scope and the breadth of what you’ve owned, not the standard of craft.

What You’ll Own

Test Infrastructure and Frameworks

* Build and own the test frameworks and harnesses our engineers use across services written in Java, Python, and TypeScript.

* Own test execution in CI: parallelisation, sharding, caching, selective test runs based on what changed, and keeping the feedback loop fast enough that engineers wait for it rather than route around it.

* Own ephemeral test environments — spun up per pull request on Kubernetes, torn down after, with the dependencies a real integration test needs.

* Build contract testing between services so integration failures surface at the boundary rather than in a staging environment nobody trusts.

* Own end-to-end and UI test infrastructure (Playwright, Cypress, or similar) and keep it stable enough to be worth having.

* Build the performance and load testing capability, so a change that degrades latency is caught before a client notices.

Test Data and Environments

* Own test data as a first-class problem: realistic financial fixtures, portfolio and fund structures, multi-currency and multi-period cases, and the edge cases that break naive assumptions.

* Build data generation and anonymisation tooling so teams can test against realistic data without touching real client data. Confidentiality here is not negotiable.

* Manage environment parity and seeding, so a test that passes in CI means something about production.

* Own the lifecycle: refresh, reset, versioning, and cleanup, so test data doesn’t quietly rot into something nobody trusts.

Quality Signals and Flakiness

* Treat flakiness as a defect in the platform, not an inconvenience. Detect it, quantify it, quarantine it, and drive it down with data.

* Own the quality signals engineering runs on: coverage where it’s meaningful, test suite duration, failure rates, escaped defects, and change failure rate.

* Make those signals visible and useful to engineering managers and product leadership, and report honestly when the trend is going the wrong way.

* Analyse escaped defects to find the gap in the testing strategy rather than the person who missed it.

* Work with SRE so pre-production quality signals and production reliability data tell one coherent story.

Testing Probabilistic and AI-Enabled Features

* Build the test infrastructure for AI-enabled features, where the same input can produce different valid outputs and assert-equals stops working.

* Implement the techniques that do work: snapshot and tolerance-based assertions, schema and constraint validation, property-based testing, and deterministic seams around non-deterministic components.

* Build the infrastructure that AI evaluation runs on — harness execution, dataset management, and CI integration — in partnership with our AI Evaluation Engineer, who owns eval methodology and scoring.

* Help teams draw the line clearly between what a deterministic test should assert and what belongs in an eval suite.

Enablement and Practice

* Enable teams to own their own testing. Build the tooling, set the patterns, and hand it over rather than becoming the team that tests everything.

* Define and champion the testing strategy across engineering: what belongs in unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, and eval, and why the shape of that pyramid matters.

* Train engineers and test engineers on testing practice, including testing probabilistic systems, which needs to be taught as its own discipline.

* Review test approaches at design time and ask how a feature will be verified before it’s built, not after.

* Write documentation and reference implementations people copy.

What You Bring

* Hands-on engineering experience building test infrastructure, automation frameworks, or developer tooling. This is a software engineering role and you’ll be judged on the code you write.

* Strong programming ability in at least one of Python, Java, or TypeScript, and comfort reading all three. Our services span them.

* Real experience owning test automation in CI/CD, including the unglamorous work of making a slow, flaky suite fast and trustworthy.

* Working knowledge of Kubernetes and containers, enough to build and debug ephemeral environments.

* Experience with test data management, particularly where privacy or confidentiality constrains what you can use.

* Demonstrated experience with contract, integration, and end-to-end testing across a distributed system, and clear judgement about what belongs at each level.

* Familiarity with performance and load testing, and with reading the results properly.

* Interest in testing AI-enabled features, and an understanding of why non-determinism breaks conventional assertions. Prior experience here is a strong plus rather than a requirement.

* A platform mindset. You measure your work by what other engineers can do without you.

* Experience in a scaleup where you had to raise the quality bar while the product and team were still growing.

* Tool-agnostic judgement. We name our stack, but we’d rather hire someone who picks the right tool than someone who defends a favourite.

* FinTech or financial services experience is a plus. Willingness to understand what a correct financial output looks like is not optional — you can’t design good fixtures for a domain you don’t understand.

* Clear communication. You can write a testing strategy engineers will follow and explain a quality trend to leadership without over-simplifying it.

How You Work With AI

We’re an AI-first company, and that has to mean something more than having a coding assistant installed. We expect engineers here to have genuinely changed how they work.

* You use AI as a working tool across the job: generating test cases and edge-case fixtures, exploring untested paths in unfamiliar code, triaging failures and clustering flaky tests, drafting test plans, and writing the documentation nobody else wants to write.

* You go beyond prompt-and-paste. You’ve built or configured something (agentic workflows, automated triage or review, evaluation harnesses, custom tooling, MCP integrations) that made a repeatable part of engineering measurably faster or more reliable.

* You know where AI output cannot be trusted. A generated test that asserts the current behaviour rather than the correct behaviour locks in the bug. You verify, you review, and you can explain how you verified.

* You apply the same scrutiny to AI-generated tests as to any pull request: read it, challenge it, own it once you ship it.

* You share what works. A technique you discovered that stays on your machine is worth a fraction of one the whole team adopts.

If your answer to “how do you use AI” is autocomplete and the occasional chat window, this role will feel like a stretch — and we’d rather tell you that now.

You Will Excel If You...

* Question everything. A test suite with high coverage and no assertions, a flaky test everyone retries, a staging environment nobody believes: you raise it rather than work around it.

* Believe a slow test suite is a correctness problem, because engineers stop running it.

* Would rather build the tooling ten teams use than test ten teams’ features yourself.

* Find flaky-test investigation satisfying rather than tedious.

* Care that the numbers are right, because in our business a wrong number reaches an investment committee.

* Are comfortable owning something end to end, including the pager for the platform you build.

* Know the difference between pragmatic and sloppy, and won’t compromise on the former to avoid the latter.

# Software Engineer, AI Product Engineering

**OVERVIEW OF 73 STRINGS:**

73 Strings is an innovative platform providing comprehensive data extraction, monitoring, and valuation solutions for the private capital industry. The company's AI-powered platform streamlines middle-office processes for alternative investments, enabling seamless data structuring and standardization, monitoring, and fair value estimation at the click of a button. 73 Strings serves clients globally across various strategies, including Private Equity, Growth Equity, Venture Capital, Infrastructure and Private Credit.

Our 2025 $55M Series B, the largest in the industry, was led by Goldman Sachs, with participation from Golub Capital and Hamilton Lane, with continued support from Blackstone, Fidelity International Strategic Ventures and Broadhaven Ventures.

Role Summary

We’re hiring software engineers at mid-level and senior to build the AI features our clients use to run post-investment operations: extracting financial data from documents, monitoring portfolios, and producing auditable valuations. These are the features people buy us for, and they’re the ones where getting it wrong is most expensive.

AI is not a side project here and not an option. It shapes how we build, and it is what we ship. That means writing the deterministic machinery around probabilistic components, deciding where an agent belongs and where it absolutely does not, and building the evaluation and guardrails that let a finance professional trust an output enough to put their name on it.

These are full-stack roles weighted toward the backend. You’ll design systems, build the services behind them, and take the feature through the UI where it lands. You’ll work directly with product leadership and with engineers across our verticals, and senior hires will drive technical initiatives that reach beyond their own team.

What You’ll Own

Building AI-Enabled Product Features

* Design and ship user-facing features built on LLMs, retrieval, extraction models, and agentic workflows, from the first prototype through to something our clients depend on quarterly.

* Own the full path of a feature: data in, model or agent in the middle, deterministic validation around it, and an interface that makes the output reviewable by a human who has to sign off on it.

* Build the evaluation harnesses, regression suites, and offline test sets that tell you whether a change made the feature better or just different.

* Design for the failure modes that matter with probabilistic systems: hallucinated values, silent low-confidence outputs, prompt injection through client documents, and drift after a model upgrade.

* Instrument features for quality in production — confidence, correction rates, human overrides, latency, cost per run — and act on what the numbers say.

Deterministic vs Agentic: Drawing the Line

* Decide, deliberately and defensibly, which parts of a system must be deterministic and which can be probabilistic. Arithmetic, audit trails, permissions, and reconciliation are not places for a model to improvise.

* Keep probabilistic components inside deterministic boundaries: schema-constrained outputs, validation, reconciliation against source data, and a clear path to human review.

* Push back on agentic designs that add nondeterminism without adding value, and make the case with reasoning rather than preference.

* Make the reasoning visible in design docs, so the next engineer understands why a step is a rule and not a prompt.

System Design and Domain Modeling

* Design services and system boundaries that reflect the business domain rather than the current org chart or the shape of last year’s database.

* Apply domain-driven design in practice: bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language, and context mapping between teams. We expect you to have used it, not just read about it.

* Model the private capital domain carefully — funds, portfolio companies, positions, valuations, as-of dates, restatements — and keep the model honest as the product grows.

* Own your services end to end: implementation, tests, CI/CD, deployment, observability, and the on-call that comes with them.

Collaboration and Technical Leadership

* Work directly with product leadership to shape what gets built, challenge assumptions, and turn a vague opportunity into a scoped, shippable feature.

* Partner with Data Engineering, ML, and other product verticals on contracts and interfaces so the same problem doesn’t get solved three times.

* Drive technical initiatives across the domain, not just within your team: shared patterns for AI features, evaluation tooling, domain models, or the standards that keep our services consistent.

* Raise the bar around you through design review, code review, and mentorship. Senior engineers here are expected to make other engineers better.

* Write clearly. A design doc that survives review is part of the job.

What You Bring

* Strong software engineering experience with production ownership of what you build. We hire at mid-level and senior; what differs is scope and the breadth of what you’ve led, not the standard of craft.

* Full-stack capability with real depth on the backend. You can design a service, reason about its failure modes, and still build the interface where the feature lands.

* Demonstrated system design ability: you can take an ambiguous problem, propose two or three viable architectures, and explain the trade-offs without hiding behind diagrams.

* Strong practical understanding of domain-driven design, and the judgement to know when a lighter approach is the right call.

* Language-agnostic engineering strength. We use TypeScript, Java, and Python, and you should be productive in at least one of them and willing to work across all three. We care that you understand systems, not that you’ve specialised in our stack.

* Hands-on experience building with LLMs or other probabilistic components in a product context: prompting and context design, retrieval, structured output, tool and function calling, agent orchestration, and evaluation.

* A clear point of view on where AI belongs in a system and where it doesn’t, formed by having shipped something and watched it behave in production.

* Comfort with modern delivery practice: automated testing, CI/CD, containers and Kubernetes, and observability as a first-class concern.

* Strong business sense. You understand who uses what you build and why it matters to them, and you make trade-offs accordingly. SaaS or FinTech experience is not required; curiosity about the domain and the discipline to learn it is.

* Self-direction. You find the important work, scope it, and drive it without waiting for a ticket.

* Experience in a fast-growing company where the roadmap, the team, and the requirements all change at once is a strong plus.

How You Work With AI

We’re an AI-first company, and that has to mean something more than having a coding assistant installed. We expect engineers here to have genuinely changed how they work.

* You use AI as a working tool across the job, not just in the editor: exploring unfamiliar code and data, generating test cases and edge-case inputs, drafting and reviewing designs, triaging production issues, and writing the documentation nobody else wants to write.

* You go beyond prompt-and-paste. You’ve built or configured something (agentic workflows, evaluation harnesses, custom tooling, MCP integrations, automated review or triage) that made a repeatable part of engineering measurably faster or more reliable.

* You know where AI output cannot be trusted. Generated code that handles the happy path and silently drops errors is worse than no code at all. You verify, you test, and you can explain how you verified.

* You apply the same judgement to AI-generated code that you’d apply to a junior engineer’s pull request: read it, challenge it, own it once you ship it.

* You share what works. A technique you discovered that stays on your machine is worth a fraction of one the whole team adopts.

If your answer to “how do you use AI” is autocomplete and the occasional chat window, this role will feel like a stretch — and we’d rather tell you that now.

You Will Excel If You...

* Question everything. A prompt standing in for business logic, a metric nobody can define, an agent added because agents are interesting: you raise it rather than build it.

* Believe a feature isn’t done until someone can trust its output without checking every row.

* Are comfortable holding both the domain model and this sprint’s delivery reality in your head at the same time.

* Enjoy working with product leadership rather than waiting for a finished spec.

* Care that the numbers are right, because in our business a wrong number reaches an investment committee.

* Know the difference between pragmatic and sloppy, and won’t compromise on the former to avoid the latter.

### **Backend Engineer - Platform - Stacks**

**This role is available for candidates located in the UK, Germany, Spain, Ireland and Sweden.**

**The Opportunity:**

Application Core Services (AppCore) is a group within Platform, in the Foundations department. Foundations produces the Internal Engineering Platform (IEP) and partners closely with our Cloud, Enterprise, and Grafana teams. Our team develops the essential systems driving Grafana's business operations. We utilize the grafana.com platform to engineer bespoke integrations and solutions that unify the diverse technical ecosystem of a modern software enterprise.

The team owns important domain areas that help keep both our customer workflows and internal business processes running smoothly. AppCore is made up of multiple squads, each focused on one or more of these domains. Our work includes maintaining the billing engine responsible for customer usage calculation, automating provisioning after a customer signs a contract, integrating with cloud marketplaces such as AWS, Azure, and GCP, and building and maintaining the user portal our customers rely on to manage their accounts.

This is a team working at the intersection of product, platform, and business operations. The systems we build are critical to how Grafana scales. We are looking for engineers who enjoy solving complex workflow and systems problems, improving reliability and developer experience, and building software that directly supports both customers and internal stakeholders.

As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. Engineers at Grafana also have the opportunity to contribute to Open Source communities and collaborate across teams beyond their immediate scope.

**What You’ll Be Doing:**

The AppCore Stacks squad owns the systems that create, configure, reconcile, migrate, and operate Grafana Cloud stacks at scale. A stack is the customer-facing Grafana Cloud environment that connects an organization to Grafana and the backend services it uses, including Mimir, Loki, Tempo, plugins, dashboards, data sources, and stack-level configuration.

Our work sits at the intersection of product, platform, and operations. We build the control-plane services and workflows that keep stack state aligned across grafana.com, Stack State Service (SSS), Hosted Grafana, cloud regions, and the underlying Grafana Cloud infrastructure. When this domain works well, customers get reliable stack creation, safe configuration rollout, predictable migrations, and fewer manual operational interventions.

* Design, build, and operate reconciliation systems, including the SSS backend, to track desired stack state, detect and repair drift across stack templates, grafana.com state, Hosted Grafana, and actual customer stack configuration
* Collaborate across SSS, grafana.com, and deployment configurations to ensure stack lifecycle workflows remain reliable, observable, and resilient
* Improve operational efficiency by reducing deployment complexity (e.g., aiming for single PR regional SSS deployment) and contributing to the Stack Config Reconciliation project
* Manage rollout mechanisms for provisioned plugins, dashboards, data sources, Grafana versions, release channels, and stack-level configuration
* Support new region and cluster rollouts, including the operational paths required to bring stacks online safely in new Grafana Cloud regions
* Improve incident response and recovery paths for stack misalignment, reconciliation failures, plugin rollout issues, and Hosted Grafana integration failures
* Partner with Product, Hosted Grafana, Infrastructure, Support, and adjacent AppCore squads on customer-impacting stack lifecycle work
* Contribute to roadmap planning, technical design, OnCall improvements, and long-term simplification of stack operations
* You will help own the production behavior of the systems you build. That includes improving runbooks, dashboards, alerts, reconciliation safety, rollout controls, and recovery procedures. Technical Direction and Engineering Standards

Building and Running AI Solutions

* Design, build and ship production ready agentic AI and automation solutions: agents that can plan, reason, use tools, retrieve information, act across our systems and hand back to a person when they should.

Owning Delivery

Working with Stakeholders and the Central AI Team

* Build inside the policies, approved tooling and guardrails the central AI team sets, and be our main point of contact with them and the AI centre of excellence so we stay aligned.

The role offers a unique perspective on the breadth of work taking place across Insurance Supervision. The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve.

At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.

We welcome applications from individuals who work flexibly, including job shares and part time working patterns. We've also partnered with external organisations to support us in making adjustments for candidates and employees in the recruitment process where they're needed.

From 1st October 2026, we expect all our colleagues to spend a minimum of 50% of their working time in the office per month. This is to capitalise on the benefits of working together in person across teams, while maintaining the flexibility offered by home working. Subject to that minimum requirement, individuals and managers should work together to find what works best for them and their team.

Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.

* Currently a non-contributory, career average pension giving you a guaranteed retirement benefit of 1/80th of your annual salary for every year worked. There is the option to increase your pension (to 1/65th) or decrease (to 1/105th) in exchange for salary through our flexible benefits programme each year.  The Bank has the discretion to vary standard accrual rates and dial up and dial down rates at any time and to withdraw dial up and dial down options at any time.
* A discretionary performance award based on a current award pool.
* An 8% benefits allowance with the option to take as salary or purchase a wide range of flexible benefits.

The Bank of England welcomes applications from all candidates, but as a UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) approved sponsor, we have a responsibility to comply with the Immigration Rules and guidance.  As such, our ability to employ individuals who require sponsorship for immigration purposes is limited.  The Bank cannot guarantee that you and / or the role you are applying for will be eligible for sponsorship and that any application made to UKVI will be successful. # Senior FP&A Analyst

Liverpool

### **About Behavox**

Behavox is a cloud-native AI company providing an integrated controls platform for global banks, asset managers, hedge funds, private equity firms, insurance businesses, and commodity firms. The platform unifies communications and trade surveillance, compliant archiving, policy management as well as front-office analytics on a single, AI-native technology stack, delivered as a globally scalable SaaS-based cloud service.

At Behavox, our engineering culture is built around speed, experimentation, and technical excellence, following agile principles and rapid iteration. We constantly test and adopt the latest cloud technologies and AI tooling, optimising for fast feedback loops and execution. We look for people who can move fast, challenge conventional wisdom, and who want to work at the frontier of modern AI, SaaS platforms, and distributed systems.

Behavox is a high-performance organisation with a strong bias toward delivery, ownership, and responsibility. We commit, and we execute. We are building systems that are complex, mission-critical, and global in scale; systems that many consider too large or too difficult. To do that, we seek the smartest, most technically capable engineers and technologists who take end-to-end responsibility and want to win by building what others cannot.

Founded in 2014 and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, Behavox is headquartered in London, with offices worldwide, including New York City, Montreal, Seattle, Singapore, and Tokyo.

### **About the Role**

The Senior FP&A Analyst owns Behavox's core financial model — its architecture, the accounting beneath it, and the forecasts and analysis the company plans and decides by. The role exists to change decisions, not report them: it turns the numbers into the choices leadership actually faces. It reads and integrates budgets into the model, but does not run the budgeting cycle.

The same analyst builds the valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma models behind every acquisition — evaluating targets, running diligence, and folding closed deals into a single consolidated view. This work is periodic and must be carried alone when it arrives; the steady state is the operating model and SaaS forecasting.

This is a high-autonomy role that works without a detailed brief and sets the modeling standard others build on. It is accountable for the accuracy and integrity of the numbers, and for turning them into recommendations sharp enough to act on — the downside case included, not just the point estimate — for senior leadership, the board, and investors. It pressure-tests the assumptions behind every result, works fluently with modern tooling and AI, and compounds that edge by learning relentlessly. Its influence comes from the rigor and reach of the analysis, not from authority: it owns the model and the truth it tells, not the decisions made from it.

### **What You'll Bring**

1. **Financial Model & Accounting Foundations** — Understands the architecture of integrated three-statement and operating models and the accounting that underpins them, including SaaS revenue recognition and cost treatment. Understands how the company's budgets are built and how to integrate them accurately into the core financial model.
2. **Forecasting & SaaS Unit Economics** — Understands bottom-up short-term forecasting, driver-based long-term modeling, and the SaaS metrics that reveal business performance. Connects movements in those metrics to their underlying drivers and the operating levers that can change them.
3. **Mergers, Acquisitions & Integration** — Understands acquisition valuation, purchase accounting, combined-entity projections, and consolidation mechanics sufficiently to evaluate targets and integrate completed acquisitions into the financial model.
4. **Business & Commercial Acumen** — Understands in depth how the business and its functions generate revenue and incur costs, including the underlying revenue drivers, cost structure, and operating levers. Applies this knowledge to identify inconsistencies and challenge financial results and assumptions.
5. **Financial Systems & AI Tooling** — Understands Google Sheets, Excel, AI, and automation capabilities sufficiently to determine how they should be applied to financial modeling and analysis. Distinguishes where automation can improve speed and control from where financial judgment and manual validation must remain.

### **What You'll Do**

1. **Financial Model Ownership** — Builds and maintains the core three-statement and operating model using robust architecture, accounting logic, scenario and sensitivity layers, and integrated budgets, owning the accuracy of every output and the integrity of every assumption to provide reliable forecasts and analysis for company planning and decision-making.
2. **Acquisition Modeling & Integration** — Builds valuations, scenarios, and pro-forma combined-entity models by independently evaluating targets, supporting due diligence, and consolidating closed deals to provide a complete financial view of acquisition implications and the combined business.
3. **Business-Review Reporting** — Drives the financial substance of monthly, quarterly, and annual business reviews with the broader FP&A team by translating model outputs and performance drivers into a clear narrative that enables senior management, the board, and investors to understand results and their implications.
4. **Metrics Analysis & Business Partnering** — Diagnoses financial and SaaS metric movements by identifying operating drivers, pressure-testing assumptions, and modeling relevant levers and downside cases to give decision-makers evidence-based recommendations they can act on.
5. **AI-Enabled Productivity** — Applies AI and spreadsheet automation to recurring financial workflows by automating appropriate work and strengthening data validation while retaining judgment over what remains manual to reduce cycle time without compromising financial integrity.

### **What We Offer**

* The opportunity to work on a global, mission-critical AI platform alongside the best engineers and technologists across multiple geographies
* A role with real ownership and impact, building complex systems at scale in an environment that values speed, experimentation, and technical excellence
* A highly attractive benefits package, including competitive cash compensation, an equity award aligned with long-term value creation, and comprehensive health insurance for employees and their families
* A generous time-off policy of 30 days annually, plus public holidays and sick leave, recognizing the importance of sustained high performance

# Lead Engineer

## **London (Hybrid) | Full-time | £100k – £130k + early-team equity**

## **The role**

We're a well-funded startup building AI for architecture, engineering and construction: an archaic, trillion-dollar industry at a critical juncture. In the UK, the Building Safety Act is one of the most significant overhauls of how buildings are designed of this generation. Directors of AEC firms now carry personal liability for design decisions. We're building the system of record that lets them prove those decisions were sound.

You'll run engineering at Bite, reporting to and working alongside El-Amin, our CTO and a former practising structural engineer. You and El-Amin will shape technical direction together: he brings deep domain expertise on how engineers reason about a column, a load path or a revision, but the platform's architecture, and how it gets built and shipped, are yours to own. The foundations are in production and the platform is polyglot by design: a Node/TypeScript backend API, a React frontend, a C#/WPF Windows desktop connector and Python ML/RAG workers on Azure. You don't need experience in construction or in our exact stack. We hire for engineering judgement, and the team are polyglots who treat specific technologies as tools for tackling problems.

## **Why join Bite**

**The problem is genuinely hard.** When a structural engineer changes Column C7 in their analysis model, the same column exists in drawings, schedules, specs and emails under different names, in different formats, some of which LLMs don't understand, and with no shared identifier. Resolving those references into one canonical entity, and predicting what just went out of date, is the core of our product, and the architecture that gets us there is yours to set.

**You'll own engineering outright, not a slice of it.** There's no engineering organisation to inherit and no layer of management to negotiate with. What exists today is a working platform and a small team; the standards, the architecture, the hiring bar and the shape of the function as it grows are all genuinely open, and they're your decisions to make.

**Your work ships to people who pay.** Our product is in production with signed customers that include some of the UK's leading structural engineering firms. Work goes from a customer conversation into the hands of working engineers within days, and you'll hear directly what landed and what didn't. If you'd rather take a call with a structural engineer at 9am and ship them a fix by 5pm than sit in a product spec review, this is that job.

## **What we're building**

Bite is the platform that turns weeks of manual change-propagation work into seconds. Structural engineers work across a fragmented set of tools with no shared source of truth: ETABS models, SAFE analyses, Autodesk drawings, Excel specs, PDFs, emails. When a design changes, propagating that change across files is manual, slow and error-prone, and the errors are expensive.

Bite is the change management and audit trail layer for structural engineering: natural-language search across a project's entire file ecosystem, cross-file impact detection, and propagation of those changes to every affected file under the engineer's supervision, all running on a single engineering knowledge graph..

## **About You**

* Love learning a new domain, and shipping something within weeks that actually fixes what was broken in it.
* Own the technical direction of the platform: the knowledge graph, the entity-resolution layer, and the architecture everything else depends on.
* Hire and grow the engineering team, and set the bar that every subsequent hire is measured against.
* Establish how engineering operates as it scales: standards, code review, release, on-call, and how work gets prioritised.
* Stay hands-on where it counts, writing and reviewing code, because that's how you earn credibility with the engineers you hire.
* Work with El-Amin on how engineers reason about a column, a load path or a revision, and encode that into the data model.
* Work closely with our Head of Product to build and execute a strong product roadmap, translating design-partner feedback into shipped features, and own engineering delivery against it.
* Ship fast without breaking trust, moving quickly on new capability while protecting the reliability of a product design partners already depend on day to day.
* Bring a track record of shipping and owning production systems end to end; years matter less to us than evidence you've done it.
* Bring experience hiring, growing and leading a small engineering team, with evidence of the engineers you've developed.
* Have strong backend depth, ideally Node.js or TypeScript in production, and are comfortable reading C# and Python.
* Have experience owning architecture for distributed, event-driven systems: APIs, queues, workers, storage.
* Are outcome-focused and hands-on, with a deep understanding of what's being built and comfort in the code, even when you're not hand-writing every line yourself.
* Have genuine product sense: there's no layer of product management between engineering and customers, and you'll be on the calls directly.
* Communicate clearly across deeply technical, semi-technical and plain-language conversations: clarity is what lets a small team move fast without customers losing trust in what's shipped.
* Are kind, curious, optimistic and driven. We believe in being kind over being nice, and we give and receive constructive feedback constantly.

## **What Will Make You Stand Out**

* Building an engineering function from a handful of people into a team, and the scar tissue that comes with it.
* LLM/RAG pipelines in production: embeddings, vector search, retrieval quality measurement.
* Graph-based data models, entity resolution, or knowledge graph tooling.
* Autodesk Platform Services or AEC data formats: IFC, Revit, ETABS, SAFE or similar.
* Background in construction, structural engineering software, or document-intensive vertical SaaS.

Don't rule yourself out over the stack. We're looking for strong engineers with sound principles. Technologies are tools.

## **What you can expect from us**

* £100k–£130k and early-team equity, with exact numbers on the table at the first conversation.
* An engineering function to build, and the authority that comes with owning it.
* Technical direction that's genuinely open. The foundations exist; the decisions ahead are yours.
* Headcount to hire against, and the final say on who joins your team.
* Direct access to customers. You'll be on calls with structural engineers, not reading a summary of them.
* Founders who want to be argued with, and who value action over consensus.
* Hybrid working from our London office (3 days a week).
* A vertical you'll learn deeply: how structural engineering firms work, how AEC data formats behave, and how LLM/RAG systems hold up in production.

## **How we work**

We believe in thorough automated testing. Not strict TDD, but every PR ships with the appropriate E2E tests, unit tests or eval harnesses. We own the entire platform including its deployment and reliability, so we control our own CI and CD. The team is autonomous, multi-disciplinary and empowered. Where you'd change any of that is your call to make.

## **Inclusion at Bite**

Bite Engineering is an Equal Employment Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or any other legally protected status. We want people from all walks of life to feel valued for their individuality, thrive in our business and share a sense of belonging. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, let us know.

At Black Sun, we believe great creative work starts by finding what matters.

As a Designer, you will help turn ideas, stories and complex information into clear, engaging and beautifully crafted communications for some of the world’s leading businesses.

You will work alongside designers, Creative Directors, account teams and other specialists, contributing to projects from early creative exploration through to final delivery.

This is a role for someone with strong design foundations who wants to keep developing. You should be as interested in why something is being designed as how it looks. We want you to ask questions, contribute ideas, explore different solutions and become increasingly confident in your own creative judgement.

You will have support and direction from more experienced members of the team, but we will also expect you to take ownership of your work and grow your contribution over time.

What you will do

Find what matters

Understand the brief before you begin designing.

* Take time to understand the client, audience, content and purpose of the work.
* Ask questions when something is unclear and start to recognise what information matters most.
* Look beyond what you have been given and bring useful references, observations and inspiration into the creative process.

Have an idea

Contribute to creative exploration rather than simply waiting for a design direction.

* Develop and share ideas, sketches and visual approaches.
* Explore different ways to solve a problem rather than settling immediately on the most obvious answer.
* Understand the idea behind the work and help maintain it as the project develops.

Make complexity clear

Turn content, data and information into communication that is easy to understand and navigate.

* Use typography, hierarchy, layout, imagery and information design to help tell the story.
* Create charts, diagrams and other visualisations that make information clearer rather than simply more decorative.
* Develop your ability to recognise what should lead, what should support and what can be simplified.

Make every choice for a reason

Create thoughtful, well crafted design across print and digital projects.

* Apply strong design fundamentals including typography, composition, colour, imagery and layout.
* Work confidently within established brand and design systems while recognising opportunities to explore and develop them.
* Prepare accurate, well organised files and work closely with publishing and production colleagues through to delivery.
* Respond positively to creative direction and feedback, understanding why changes are being made rather than simply making them.
* Build confidence with new tools and creative possibilities, including motion, digital, AI and emerging technologies where they can strengthen the work.

Make a difference

Take pride in the quality of everything you produce.

* Be curious about whether the work is communicating effectively, not simply whether it looks good.

Job Description

  

**The role**

This is a senior opportunity to join and lead the London Corporate Transactions & Advisory (**CT&A**) Product Group's existing Knowledge & Training and Thought Leadership team (**K&T and TL team**), consisting of experienced Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists.

Our London CT&A Product Group advises on some of the world's largest and most complex M&A transactions, including private M&A, joint ventures, restructurings and corporate advisory work.

Our K&T and TL team is focused on delivering practical and insightful knowhow and advice to lawyers, predominantly in London but also across our global network.  Key to achieving this goal is the need to keep abreast of legal and regulatory developments and work closely with our lawyers in order to ensure that deal and advisory knowhow and insights are collated, analysed and shared across the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.

In summary, you will be responsible for ensuring that the London CT&A K&T and TL team delivers on ensuring that lawyers have legal and regulatory knowledge and knowhow at their fingertips, whether that is internal knowhow or knowledge on legal and regulatory developments.

In addition, your particular area of expertise will be company law and corporate governance.  You will keep up to date with, and analyse, all legal and regulatory developments in respect of these areas.  You will also be the "go to" resource for legal and regulatory developments, template maintenance and production, knowledge sharing, training, thought leadership, client communications and AI and innovation in respect of company law and corporate governance.

Your role will also play an important part by ensuring our collective experience is captured and utilised for the benefit of all across the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.

You will provide valuable support to the Chair of the CLLS Company Law Committee and any partner on the Company Law Committee of the Law Society, which will involve taking part in working groups, alongside members of these Committees, formed to respond to Government and regulatory body consultations that impact the work of the CT&A Product Group, with a particular focus on company law and corporate governance.

You will also help drive the adoption of legal technology, including the firm's AI tools, by fee earners.  By combining this focus with your legal expertise, you will support the delivery of more efficient, consistent and client-focused legal services.

**Who you will work with**

You will work in our leading, world-class CT&A Global Product Group, alongside the partners and lawyers.

What makes us one of the most respected Corporate Transactions & Advisory practices globally is our client base, the mandates we win, our industry expertise and commercial approach, and our people and their intellectual capability.  We are consistently retained as lead international counsel on cross-border mandates and our team has a diverse client base that includes a number of FTSE350 and Fortune 500 listed corporations.

You will work within the London CT&A Product Group and also be part of our London and global K&T and TL teams.  This means you will work collaboratively with Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in other Product Groups in the London office (including Private Equity, Debt Finance, Employment, Incentives and Real Estate) and in our offices across the globe.

The role more generally and the work supporting the partners involved with the CLLS and Law Society Company Law Committees will provide opportunities to interact with other City law firms, Government departments such as the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) and industry bodies/regulators such as the FCA, the Takeover Panel, Companies House and the FRC.

You will also collaborate with our Corporate Governance Team, Business Development Team, Transformation Team and Legal Technology Advisors.  Clifford Chance's Transformation Team and Legal Technology Advisors work collaboratively with fee earners and Knowledge Lawyers to deliver the highest-quality, efficient and cost-effective client service, including by leveraging developments in AI and legal technology.

**What you will be responsible for**

**Leading London CT&A K&T and TL team**

* Managing the CT&A Knowledge Lawyer team, with responsibility for appraisal reviews, objective setting, performance management and monitoring progress against strategic priorities.
* Leading CT&A K&T and TL business planning, including setting the strategic direction for the CT&A K&T and TL team and overseeing implementation of the business plan.
* Leading on ensuring effective collaboration with the Corporate Governance Team on relevant legal and regulatory developments.
* Running the London Corporate Knowhow Committee, including liaising with Knowledge Lawyers and the Corporate Governance Team, preparing and circulating agenda and supporting information, facilitating meetings and ensuring appropriate follow-up.

**Legal/regulatory**

* Analysing forthcoming legal/regulatory developments in respect of company law and corporate governance in order to update lawyers and clients on their impact (including supporting the team, led by our Corporate Governance specialists, that prepares a corporate governance update emailed to clients on a weekly basis and preparing other client communications and client presentation materials) and to update internal resources e.g. templates/practice notes/Topic Guides.
* Responding to fee earner queries on legal/regulatory matters in respect of company law and corporate governance, including on legal/regulatory developments.
* Contributing to legal/regulatory consultation responses relevant to company law and corporate governance.
* Supporting Clifford Chance partners on work relating to external legal committees, such as the Company Law Committees of the CLLS and the Law Society.
* Preparing and presenting summaries on legal/regulatory developments in respect of company law and corporate governance at London Corporate Knowhow Committee meetings.

**Knowledge management and sharing**

* Maintaining an up-to-date knowledge database, ensuring content is well curated, structured and optimised for effective use with the firm’s AI tools.
* Encouraging fee earners to share and submit knowhow to the firm's knowledge database.
* Assisting with the development and maintenance of any relevant bespoke knowhow collections.
* Identifying improved ways to capture, organise and share knowhow.

**Templates**

* Maintaining, reviewing and updating existing company law and corporate governance templates to ensure they remain accurate, current and aligned with legal, regulatory and market developments.
* Identifying and creating new company law and corporate governance templates as required.
* Improving the accessibility and ease of use of company law and corporate governance templates, including through template automation and optimisation for effective use with the firm’s AI tools.

**Training**

* Preparing and/or delivering training on company law and corporate governance, including legal/regulatory developments in these areas.
* Delivering knowledge updates on company law and corporate governance to the CT&A Product Group as well as other relevant Product Groups within the firm.

**AI and innovation**

* Supporting the development, adoption and effective use of legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, across the London office and globally, helping to share best practice and embed new ways of working.
* Promoting and assisting fee earners with the use of legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, and helping to identify and develop appropriate use cases to improve matter delivery and lawyer productivity.
* Supporting the responsible use of the firm's legal technology tools, including the firm’s AI tools, in line with firm policies, client requirements and confidentiality obligations.

**Collaboration**

* Collaborating with Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in Product Groups that deliver M&A and corporate advisory client work to ensure activities are co-ordinated in respect of legal, regulatory and market practice developments, knowledge management, training, thought leadership and AI/innovation.
* Collaborating with other Knowledge Lawyers and information specialists in London and globally to ensure knowledge is shared and activities are co-ordinated within Product Groups globally and across other relevant Product Groups within the firm, particularly in respect of company law and corporate governance.
* Participating in external Knowledge Lawyer community discussions to share knowledge and information on legal and regulatory topics as well as market practice.

  

Qualifications

  

**Your experience**

You will be an existing Knowledge Lawyer (PSL) (with significant senior experience in company law and corporate governance.  Experience in M&A (including private M&A, joint ventures and reorganisations) would be beneficial.

You will have strong drafting skills, good attention to detail and strong organisational skills.  You will also be proactive and committed to providing a first class service to our lawyers and clients.

You should have strong leadership, communication and analytical skills, along with a high level of commercial awareness.  You should also have a strong track record of keeping abreast of legal and regulatory developments.

You should also have a strong interest in legal technology, AI and innovation and prior experience in this area would be beneficial.

  

Company Description

  

**Who we are**

As a global law firm our work spans jurisdictions, cultures, and languages – and so do our people.

Our culture is collaborative and inclusive — where diverse perspectives are recognised and valued. Where performing to your highest ability, unlocks equal access to opportunities to learn, thrive and grow.

We combine deep legal expertise and commercial intelligence to grow, transform, protect, and defend our clients' businesses, across every critical moment.

We operate in the sectors and regions that matter to our clients. With forward-thinking insights and innovative, tech-enabled solutions that combine deep knowledge of their sectors and markets.

Join us to build connections and work with colleagues as one global team – empowering each other to be exceptional and create advantage for our clients.

  

Additional Information

  

**How we will support you**

From your first day with us, you will have opportunities to develop your skills and knowledge through formal training, informal coaching and mentoring, technical training and on the job learning.

**Hybrid working**

This role follows our 'balanced' hybrid working approach and as long as business needs allow, you will be supported to work in a hybrid way in line with the hybrid working policy.

# Summary of the Founding Creative Director job at Siena AI

Siena AI is hiring a Founding Creative Director . Based in London, UK. Working arrangement: Remote.

## About Siena AI

Siena AI builds empathic AI agents for commerce that integrate with existing help desk and commerce systems to autonomously handle customer interactions across multiple channels. Its platform covers customer support, shopping assistance, review management, and persistent customer memory to generate actionable business insights.

## Founding Creative Director job description

## **Meet Siena**

Siena is the The Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.   
  
It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.

## 

## **The team**

We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.

We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.

If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.

## **The role**

Siena is building the intelligence layer for CX, and we're about to launch several products in quick succession. We are not looking for someone to execute a brief well. We are looking for the person whose taste the rest of the company gets measured against: someone who looks at a landing page and can't not have an opinion, who would rather kill a launch than ship something mediocre, and who has owned creative direction before, not just contributed to it.

If you need a creative director above you setting the vision, a team to delegate to on day one, or a slow, considered, one-project-at-a-time pace, stop reading now. This isn't that job.

If you're the person other designers already defer to on taste, continue.

## **This is a craft title. Not a headcount title.**

You will ship personally for the first year and set the bar for everyone who comes after. Over time you will build a small internal agency, two to three people across design, motion, and content, that can brief, position, and launch without outside help.

* Narrative and positioning across every launch - design as strategy, not decoration
* Every artifact that goes to market: landing pages, launch video, decks, social
* The design system, from v3 onward
* The bar, full stop - if it ships under the Siena name, you made it or you signed off on it

## **What it takes to be in the room**

* **Taste, above everything, and evidence you can defend it.** Specific, defended opinions about what's good and why.
* **A track record of owning creative direction, not just contributing to it.** Agency or in-house, brand refresh or full launch - you've been the person whose call was final, not the one waiting on notes.
* **Narrative thinking.** Design as positioning. You should already have a point of view on how a brand like Siena should be positioned, not just how it should look.
* **AI as a working tool, not a threat to your taste.** You've already built something with AI - an app, a prototype, a mockup - and you want to get technical enough to ship a landing page yourself within a year. Anti-AI is disqualifying.
* **Range that travels.** Your background doesn't have to be SaaS. Fashion, art, consumer brand, editorial - what matters is whether your taste holds up somewhere new.
* **A pattern of shipping in chaos, not around it.** Multiple launches in flight, feedback that moves in hours not weeks. If your best work happens on a slow, protected timeline, that's useful information - it's just not this role.

## **Why this is worth it**

You're not joining a design team to fit into. You're setting the taste bar for a company that's about to be a lot more visible, a lot faster than most companies get that chance.

This is intense - real ownership, real launches, a founder team that reviews your work directly and moves at the pace you'd expect from that. It's also one of the rare creative seats where nothing you make gets diluted by committee before it ships.

If that sounds like the room you've been trying to get into, we want to talk to you.

If it sounds like too much scrutiny too fast, this isn't a knock on you - it just isn't this role.

## Why Siena?

* **Real ownership.** You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.
* **Work that ships and matters.** What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.
* **A category we are creating.** The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.
* **A team that respects your judgment.** Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.
* **Great salary plus equity or stock grants.** Own a piece of what you build.
* **Learning budget.** If you are growing, so are we.
* **AI-fluency by default.** Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.

## **Our values**

The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback—both giving and receiving it—because they care more about getting things right than being polite.

They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.

## **Our approach to AI**

The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.

Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.

At Siena, we’re not just looking for people who can do a job. We’re looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that’s you, we look forward to your application.

We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at talent@siena.cx.

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.*

AI Productivity Coach (Level 3)

**Reports to**: Delivery Director

**Location**: UK Remote, with national travel as required

**About Corndel**

Corndel is a unique, multi award-winning UK management and technology training provider that focuses on delivering the highest quality programmes throughout an employee’s career. We partner with some of the UK’s largest and most exciting businesses to help drive organisational and personal performance through transformational learning.

Our mission is to inspire people to think bigger and shape the future, and our vision is to expand minds and create a world of unlimited potential. We are one of the fastest growing companies in the UK and provide a great platform for proactive and motivated individuals to take the next exciting step in their career. You will be joining an organisation with a fun, entrepreneurial and supportive environment, providing fulfilling work and an open, informal culture.

**Purpose of the Role**

The AI3 Coach (Working Smarter with AI) exists to help learners build confidence and capability in using AI enabled digital tools safely, effectively, and responsibly in the workplace.

In this role, you will coach and support learners on Corndel’s Level 3 Working Smarter with AI programme, helping them adopt practical AI enabled workflows using Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Copilot. You will guide learners to understand not just how to use tools, but how to apply sound judgement, maintain human oversight, and improve productivity in ways that genuinely add value.

You will combine strong digital and M365 expertise with a coaching mindset, empowering learners to develop confidence, good habits, and transferable skills that support their long‐term development.

**Core Responsibilities**

**Learner Coaching & Development**

* Manage a caseload of learners, building trusted relationships through structured one‐to‐one coaching and group workshops.
* Support learners at different stages of confidence and digital maturity, adapting your approach to meet individual needs.
* Create an inclusive, psychologically safe learning environment where learners feel comfortable asking questions, practising new skills, and learning from mistakes.
* Encourage learners to take ownership of their development, building confidence through practical application and reflection.

**Digital Productivity & AI Adoption**

* Coach learners to use Microsoft 365 tools (including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, Excel and PowerPoint) to improve everyday productivity.
* Guide learners in the practical use of Microsoft Copilot and other AI tools, including promptbased approaches that enhance clarity, efficiency and decision making.
* Support learners to develop safe, ethical, and responsible AI habits, including awareness of data privacy, bias, and security considerations.
* Help learners recognise opportunities to apply AI enabled workflows in real workplace tasks, balancing innovation with good professional judgement.

**Digital Support & Problem Solving**

* Support learners to develop foundational digital support skills, such as diagnosing simple application issues, providing user support, and troubleshooting.
* Build learner understanding of organisational digital processes, escalation routes, and best practice.
* Encourage a solutions‐focused mindset, helping learners approach problems methodically and confidently.

**Progress, Quality & Outcomes**

* Guide learners through programme milestones, assessments, and portfolio evidence, ensuring consistent progress and timely completion.
* Support learners to produce high‐quality, compliant evidence that reflects genuine capability and understanding.
* Engage constructively with learners’ line managers to support progress and reinforce the value of the programme.
* Maintain high standards of quality, safeguarding, and data handling, making thoughtful decisions that prioritise learner wellbeing and success.

**Collaboration & Continuous Improvement**

* Work collaboratively with colleagues across Operations, Product, and Curriculum to deliver a consistent and high‐quality learner experience.
* Stay curious about emerging digital and AI trends, bringing relevant developments into learning conversations where they add value.
* Contribute ideas and insight to continuously improve delivery approaches and learner outcomes.

**Technical Skills & Experience**

**Essential**

* Expert working knowledge of Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
* Practical experience using Microsoft Copilot and/or other AI tools to support productivity and workflow improvement.
* Understanding of AI fundamentals, including how large language models work and how they can be applied responsibly in the workplace.
* Confidence in prompt‐based interaction with AI tools, with the ability to explain effective prompting strategies to others.
* Awareness of AI risks and limitations, including data privacy, bias, security, and responsible use.
* Experience diagnosing and resolving common application issues, with an understanding of digital support and helpdesk practices.
* Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non‐technical learners.

Desirable

* Experience with Power Automate or other low‐code/no‐code automation tools.
* Familiarity with Copilot Studio or Power Apps.
* Experience delivering training, coaching, or user support in a professional environment.
* Teaching, training, or IT support qualifications (e.g. Microsoft Certified Trainer, ITIL).

**What Success in This Role Looks Like**

In this role, success means that you:

* Consistently support learners to complete their programme and End Point Assessment successfully and on time.
* Are trusted by learners as a knowledgeable, approachable, and supportive coach.
* Enable learners to use AI‐enabled tools with confidence, judgement, and awareness of risk.
* Maintain high standards of quality, professionalism, and learner care.
* Contribute positively to a collaborative, inclusive, and high‐performing team culture.

**What Brilliant Looks Like**

At its best, this role creates impact well beyond individual sessions:

* Learners describe your support as pivotal in building their confidence with AI and digital tools.
* You spot patterns across cohorts and proactively improve learner experience and outcomes.
* You introduce practical, thoughtful ways of using AI that genuinely improve productivity and decision‐making.
* You balance encouragement with challenge, helping learners build good habits rather than shortcuts.
* Your influence supports organisations to adopt AI‐enabled productivity in a responsible, sustainable way.

**Who This Role Is For**

This role is ideal for a digital support, IT, or M365 professional who:

* Enjoys helping others develop confidence with technology.
* Is curious about AI and its practical workplace applications.
* Values integrity, inclusion, and impact alongside technical capability.
* Wants to combine professional expertise with coaching and education to make a real difference.

**Why join Corndel?**

* Work flexibly and stay connected – most of our people work remotely, supported by regular Regional Connect Days and our annual all-company Cornfest.

* See the impact of your work – every role at Corndel shapes how organisations grow, so you’ll see your contribution translate into stronger leaders and teams.

* We're a leader in our field, with quality and excellence at the heart of what we do.

We're committed to having a fully inclusive, welcoming and safe culture and always striving to improve.

# Senior Infrastructure Engineer – Projects

**Title:** Senior Implementation Engineer  
**Location:**Lowry Mill, Lees Street, Manchester, M27 6DB   
**Working pattern:** Hybrid – 3 days per week in the office, unless on-site delivering projects   
**Salary:** £50,000-£59,000   
**Hours:**Full-time, 37.5 hours per week   
**Reporting to:**Head of Technical Services

**ABOUT DATASPIRE**

Dataspire partners with schools and multi-academy trusts to build dependable, high-performing technology environments. Our work helps schools operate securely and efficiently, while enabling teachers and students to make the most of technology. We are looking for a Senior Implementation Engineer to lead the technical delivery of complex infrastructure projects across networking, wireless, firewalls, servers, virtualisation, storage and backup. You will be the technical lead on cutovers, migrations and go-live events, translating approved designs into detailed, controlled delivery plans that leave environments properly built, tested and documented. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys being on site, thrives under the pressure of a live cutover and takes genuine pride in the quality of what they hand over.

**THE ROLE**

As Senior Implementation Engineer, you will lead complex project workstreams and turn high-level designs into detailed implementation plans, task sequences, validation steps and rollback approaches. You will act as third-line escalation during project delivery, review documentation produced by other engineers to ensure it is fit for operational handover, and mentor Associate and Implementation Engineers. You will work closely with Solutions Design, the PMO and Systems Operations, and will feed lessons learned back to improve delivery standards across the function.

**TRAVEL AND SITE WORKING**

This role involves regular travel to customer sites, including schools, colleges, construction sites and building projects. Travel is predominantly across England, with occasional work in Wales and Scotland. Some projects will require overnight stays and work outside of standard hours, including school holiday periods, to minimise disruption to teaching. The following are required or may be required for this role:

* A full, valid UK driving licence and access to a vehicle
* A clean enhanced DBS check, given the nature of working in schools and colleges around children and young people
* SSSTS (Site Supervisors Safety Training Scheme) may be required for work on construction and building sites
* ECS (Electrotechnical Certification Scheme) card may be required for certain site environments

Where you do not already hold SSSTS or ECS, we will support you in obtaining these.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Lead complex project workstreams across networking, wireless, firewalls, servers, virtualisation, storage, backup and security
* Translate high-level designs into detailed implementation plans, task sequences, validation steps and rollback approaches
* Act as technical lead during cutovers, migrations and go-live events, owning success criteria, communication points and rollback options
* Configure and commission core infrastructure including switching, routing, VLANs, enterprise wireless, firewalls, server builds, hypervisors, storage and backup platforms
* Carry out structured testing, validation and evidence capture before handover
* Handle third-line escalation during project delivery
* Review documentation produced by engineers and ensure it is suitable for operational handover to Systems Operations
* Work with Project Managers and the PMO on planning, progress, change control and risk tracking
* Work with Solutions Design to clarify design intent and feedback practical improvements
* Work with Systems Operations to ensure monitoring, backup and support readiness are in place at go-live
* Identify delivery risks, dependencies and blockers early and escalate with the right information
* Mentor and coach Associate and Implementation Engineers, raising technical and documentation standards
* Contribute to implementation standards, build guides and configuration baselines
* Work safely and methodically on customer and construction sites, following site rules and safe working practices

**TECHNOLOGIES YOU WILL WORK WITH**

*Core to the role. These are the areas you will work in day to day and where we expect real depth.*

* Network and connectivity: HPE Aruba (primary estate), Cisco Meraki and Ubiquiti. Switch configuration, routing, VLANs, stacking, PoE and structured testing
* Wireless LAN: HPE Aruba and Cisco Meraki. Access point installation, controller configuration, SSID and policy setup, validation
* Security and edge services: Smoothwall, Securly, Barracuda and Fortinet. Firewall configuration, rule sets, VPN setup and security baselines
* Servers and operating systems: Windows Server, Dell EMC and HPE ProLiant. Server build, OS deployment, role configuration, testing and handover
* Virtualisation: Hyper-V, VMware ESXi and vCenter. Hypervisor build, VM provisioning, migration and testing
* Storage and backup: SAN, NAS, Storage Spaces Direct and Redstor. Storage configuration, backup platform build and restore testing
* Cabling and physical infrastructure: structured cabling, patching, fibre, PDUs and UPS

*Wider exposure. Useful but not essential. You will come across these as part of wider project delivery and where you do not have experience, we will support you to build it.*

* Identity and access: Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Azure AD and IAM Cloud
* Collaboration and productivity: Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace for Education
* Endpoint and device management: Autopilot, SCCM, Intune, Google Endpoint Management, JAMF, Lightspeed and MDM platforms
* Apple management: macOS, iPadOS, iOS and JAMF
* Remote access and communications: RDS, VPN, 3CX and Microsoft Teams
* AV and classroom technology: Promethean, Clevertouch, Prowise, Viewsonic and SMART
* Security, filtering, safeguarding and compliance technology aligned with DfE, NCSC, Cyber Essentials and KCSIE expectations

**WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR**

* Strong hands-on delivery experience across networking and server infrastructure in an MSP, education or multi-site environment
* Demonstrable hands-on experience with HPE Aruba or Cisco Meraki. The majority of our network estate is HPE Aruba, followed by Cisco, so proven configuration and deployment experience with at least one of these is essential
* Confident configuring and commissioning managed switching, routing, VLANs and enterprise wireless
* Solid firewall experience including rule sets, VPNs and applying security baselines
* Proven Windows Server build and configuration experience including core roles
* Practical virtualisation experience with Hyper-V or VMware, including VM provisioning and migration
* Experience of storage and backup implementation, including restore and recovery testing
* Demonstrable experience leading, or acting as technical lead on, cutovers, migrations or go-live events including planning rollback
* Ability to translate a high-level design into a detailed, sequenced implementation plan
* Clear, disciplined technical documentation suitable for operational handover
* A calm, structured approach under pressure, with sound judgement on when to escalate
* A full, valid UK driving licence and willingness to travel to customer sites across England, and occasionally Wales and Scotland
* Willingness to undergo an enhanced DBS check and maintain a clean record

**DESIRABLE EXPERIENCE**

* Vendor certifications in networking, server or virtualisation, for example Aruba, Cisco, Microsoft or VMware
* Experience across both HPE Aruba and Cisco Meraki rather than one
* SSSTS, ECS card or other relevant site safety qualifications
* Experience working with schools, colleges or multi-academy trusts
* Knowledge of DfE standards, NCSC guidance, KCSIE, Cyber Essentials or education safeguarding requirements
* Experience working on live construction or building site environments
* Experience mentoring, coaching or peer reviewing other engineers
* Interest in automation, scripting and repeatable build methods
* Education-sector experience is beneficial but not essential. We are equally interested in candidates who bring strong infrastructure delivery experience, with an interest in helping technology improve educational outcomes.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

* Salary of £50,000–£59,000
* Hybrid working, with 3 days per week in our Manchester office unless on site delivering projects
* 32 days’ annual leave, including bank holidays (Increases to 33 after 3 years, 34 after 4 years and 35 after 5 years)
* An additional paid Christmas shutdown day
* Your birthday off
* On-site parking
* Optional branded workwear
* Employee Assistance Programme, including wellbeing, mental health, legal, financial and personal support
* Support in obtaining site safety qualifications such as SSSTS and ECS where required

**DEVELOPMENT AND PROGRESSION**

You will benefit from a structured development framework including:

* Continuing Professional Development (CPDs) aligned to our financial year.
* Monthly 1:1s.
* Pluralsight licence with ringfenced learning time.
* Vendor-led training where needs identified.
* Clear progression path towards Principal by owning larger, riskier or multi-site projects and reviewing the work of others.

**WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS**

Every network you build, every server you commission and every cutover you lead directly affects whether a school starts the day working. The infrastructure you deliver gives teachers confidence in the technology they rely on, keeps students safe online and provides education leaders with reliable foundations for the future.
